propositions: Fourteen test modules hand-build identical nested pytest invocations, each re-deciding basetemp, timeout, cache plugin, and env, creating duplication and three separate closed bugs all rooted in missing --basetemp.
The helper run_nested_pytest must consolidate all 14 launches into a single definition that always supplies --basetemp to avoid tempdir cleanup races and liveness defects.
The helper must forward caller-supplied env mappings byte-identically without merging or widening, so four security oracles with deliberately minimal two-to-three-key env mappings remain valid.
The helper must preserve all per-site divergences in *args, cwd, timeout, and no_cacheprovider as unevaluated passthrough, leaving site-specific pytest flags and timeouts unchanged.

Three existing sites genuinely lack --basetemp today (test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py, test_git_version_floor.py, test_live_jira_xdist_confinement.py) and are live instances of the same defect.

An AST-based guard must prevent future hand-built nested pytest launches by detecting any list-or-tuple literal in tests/**/*.py containing sys.executable, '-m', 'pytest' in sequence outside the helper module itself.
